first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A wedding planning company that will organise a wedding in the US or Canada, mostly Hawaii, Napa, New York and Banff. The first thing they actually tell me is Hawaii marriage licence rules, not what they do or what it costs. Fine, it's useful, but I can get that from the Hawaii government site I already have open.

attention_map.quote: Wedded Concierge pairs you with a Wedded Advisor who plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance.
attention_map.why: Clear enough. 'Last dance' sounds like someone is there on the night. I noted that to check later, and further down the page says something different.

attention_map.quote: Legal and entry rules from official government sites, checked October 2026.
attention_map.why: This is sitting where I'd expect proof about the company. It's proof the government exists. It tells me nothing about whether these people have ever pulled off a wedding in Maui.

attention_map.quote: Few regions change this much in one flight.
attention_map.why: Brochure filler. Same with "dinner in the city that never needs a backdrop" and "slow gold late afternoons in Hawaii". "A grand hotel above a lake that freezes in winter" and then "A winter wedding in a grand hotel above a frozen lake" is the same line said twice. Nothing here I couldn't read on any travel listicle.

attention_map.quote: Hawaii, California and the places couples ask about most: Napa, New York City, Colorado, Charleston, New Orleans and Las Vegas.
attention_map.why: The next section says it's comparing "the places couples ask about most" too, and that list is different: Kauai, Big Sur and Banff are in, New Orleans is out. The Canada card sells Vancouver and Toronto, but neither is in the comparison table or the form's Place list. So which is it?

attention_map.quote: Rules set by California; we check them for your date
attention_map.why: Six of the ten rows say a version of this. That's a column that says nothing. "City weekends for any age" and "Adults-led dinners; families welcome" are the kind of fit notes that fit anything. No price column at all, so this isn't a like-for-like comparison of anything I care about.

attention_map.quote: Collect the licence no sooner than 30 days before the ceremony. There is no waiting period once it is issued, and it is valid for 30 days, in Hawaii only.
attention_map.why: Specific, sourced, dated, and the numbers line up with the hero and the FAQs. Best part of the page. It still doesn't tell me why I need a planner for it.

attention_map.quote: Check ESTA eligibility on the official US site before flying to the US, and check eTA rules on the official Canadian site before flying to Canada.
attention_map.why: The meta description promised travel rules for AU passports. The AU line is homework. Worse, the FAQ says flatly that guests from Australia "need travel authorisation before flying", so one part of the page knows the answer and another tells me to go look it up. Also the table caption says "Entry rules for every passport" when there are three.

attention_map.quote: Hawaii, the mainland coasts, the mountains and Canada each run on different seasons. Tell us your month and we check weather, rates and availability for it.
attention_map.why: A heading called 'at a glance' with nothing to glance at. Repeated almost word for word in the FAQ. Every vague answer on this page ends in 'tell us and we check'.

attention_map.quote: What will it cost? See what drives the budget in the answers below.
attention_map.why: I clicked straight to this. It sends me to an FAQ with no numbers.

attention_map.quote: Weddings we have featured across the region
attention_map.why: 'Featured' is not 'planned'. Did they plan any of these or just write them up? That word matters to me and they've chosen the soft one.

attention_map.quote: a Maui stay that brings every generation together.
Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact: they explain your options, the legal route for your passports and what drives cost.
attention_map.why: One contact is a real reason. But the steps stop at "Plan the guest experience". Nothing about the day itself, after the hero promised the last dance.

attention_map.quote: One advisor plans the whole celebration with you, from the first call to the guest list.
attention_map.why: Up top it was "first enquiry to the last dance". Here it's "first call to the guest list". Those are different jobs. The Marketplace card says "Browse partner venues and suppliers" with nothing to browse. And now there's Wedded Concierge, Wedded Advisor, Wedded Privileges and a Wonderland Studio. Too many names for one service.

attention_map.quote: Inside Darius Slayton and Anna Hall's castle wedding in New York
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip on a page where I'm trying to work out if I trust you with my money. Makes this feel like a magazine, not a planner.

attention_map.quote: Hawaii draws more searches than any other US wedding destination we track
attention_map.why: 'We track' how? Unproven claim, first line of the FAQ. The all-inclusive answer is the most honest thing on the page ("the total depends on what you choose. We explain each line before you commit") but it stops short of telling me what a line looks like. The budget answer, "the place, the season, your guest count and how far your guests fly", is something I already knew.

When? No timeframe here or in the success message ("We will be in touch"). Place list doesn't include New Orleans, Vancouver or Toronto, all named earlier. 'Hawaii' as a separate option next to 'United States' is odd too.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: No price anywhere. The budget FAQ lists four cost drivers and no figures; the all-inclusive FAQ says the total 'depends on what you choose'. No inclusions or exclusions list.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: Hawaii licence facts are consistent everywhere (no residency rule, no waiting period, 30 days). Not consistent: 'places couples ask about most' lists differ between s2 and s3; Vancouver, Toronto and New Orleans are promoted then missing from the table and form; AU travel is stated as fact in FAQ 2 but hedged in the passport section; service scope is 'to the last dance' in s1 and s7 but 'to the guest list' in s8; 'every passport' covers three.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: No venue is named as one they've worked with. Real weddings are 'weddings we have featured', not weddings they planned. The proof strip shows government sources, not track record.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: 'Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact' and they check licence and entry rules for every passport in the group. That's a reason, but the legal steps are already laid out free on this page with government links, so it undercuts itself.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Nothing about the day itself. The 'last dance' line implies presence; the How it works steps end before the wedding.

objections_triggered.objection: Inconsistent lists: the page names different 'most asked about' places in two sections, and promotes places (Vancouver, Toronto, New Orleans) that then vanish from the comparison table and the enquiry form
objections_triggered.triggered_by: s2 'the places couples ask about most: Napa, New York City, Colorado, Charleston, New Orleans and Las Vegas' vs s3 'Compare the places couples ask about most' (Kauai, Big Sur in, New Orleans out); Canada card 'Vancouver on the coast and Toronto'

objections_triggered.objection: Contradiction on AU travel: one section says AU guests need authorisation, another tells me to go check
objections_triggered.triggered_by: FAQ 2 'For guests from Australia or the UK, both countries ... need travel authorisation before flying' vs s3 and FAQ 6 'check ESTA eligibility on the official US site'
s1 and s7 'from the first enquiry to the last dance' vs s8 'from the first call to the guest list'
FAQ 1 'Hawaii draws more searches than any other US wedding destination we track'; s5 'Weddings we have featured' (featured, not planned); proof strip that proves only that government websites exist

objections_triggered.objection: Vague answers that all end in 'tell us and we check'
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Rules set by California; we check them for your date' (six table rows); 'each run on different seasons. Tell us your month' (twice); budget FAQ with drivers only

objections_triggered.objection: Promised content not delivered: meta promises AU passport travel rules; 'Seasons at a glance' has nothing to glance at; Marketplace says 'Browse' with nothing to browse
objections_triggered.triggered_by: meta 'travel rules for US, UK and AU passports'; 'Seasons at a glance'; 'Browse partner venues and suppliers in the United States and Canada'
Table caption 'Entry rules for every passport are in "Travel by passport" below' (only US, UK, AU)
'A Wedded Advisor replies.' and 'We will be in touch'

trust_signals_noticed: Hawaii licence steps with official source link and 'Last checked October 2026'
Hawaii facts repeat consistently in hero, table, spotlight and FAQs
Passport rules linked to US State Department and GOV.UK
'Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact'
'We explain each line before you commit' in the all-inclusive FAQ
No urgency tactics, no countdowns, no 'limited spots'
turn_offs_noticed: Brochure filler in the spotlight: 'Few regions change this much in one flight', 'the city that never needs a backdrop', 'slow gold late afternoons'
Same line twice: 'a lake that freezes in winter' / 'a grand hotel above a frozen lake'
Celebrity 'Trending' posts on a planning page
Too many brand names: Wedded Concierge, Wedded Advisor, Wedded Privileges, Wonderland Studio
Proof strip with no proof about the company

emotional_response.overall: Mildly reassured by the legal detail, then increasingly suspicious as the same 'tell us and we check' line covered every hard question.
emotional_response.fear_of_hidden_costs: unchanged; nothing on the page reduced it

payload.decision_reason: Known gaps (no price or inclusions, no fee model, no proof numbers, nothing about on the day) would have kept me from enquiring on their own. But the copy itself also gave me reasons to say no: the 'most asked about' places change between sections and the Canada cities vanish from the table and form, the FAQ says AU guests need travel authorisation while the passport section tells me to go check, and the service runs 'to the last dance' in one place and 'to the guest list' in another. My rule is I don't enquire while any inconsistency is still open. The Hawaii licence section is good, but it's free on the government site and doesn't show me why I need these people. The other tabs win this week.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Okay, the Hawaii licence bit is solid, I'll give them that. Everything else is 'tell us and we'll check'. Rules? We'll check. Seasons? Tell us your month. Cost? It depends on the place, the season, your guests and flights. Yes, I know. Then the places list changes between two sections, Vancouver and Toronto get a card and then disappear, and the FAQ tells me Aussies need authorisation right after another bit told me to go look it up myself. 'Weddings we have featured', so did you plan them or not? And one line says you're with me to the last dance and another says to the guest list. What's the catch? I can't tell, and that's the problem. Closing the tab.
